territorial_scope.description: A Florida state statute that creates a state advisory council and state criminal offenses and amends the Florida Statutes.

evidence.quote: Be It Enacted by the Legislature of the State of Florida:

summary.short: Florida SB 1680 (2024) creates a Government Technology Modernization Council to study and recommend on AI and government technology, and makes knowingly possessing or intentionally creating generated child pornography a third-degree felony. Effective July 1, 2024.
summary.long: SB 1680 (2024) makes three changes to Florida law. Section 1 creates s. 282.802, F.S., establishing the Government Technology Modernization Council as an advisory council within the Department of Management Services, with state officials, appointed experts and legislators as members. The council meets at least quarterly to study new technologies, including automated decision systems, AI safety standards, digital provenance disclosure for generated images and audio, and bad-actor uses of AI, and must submit legislative recommendations to the Governor and legislative leaders by December 31, 2024 and each December 31 thereafter. Section 2 creates s. 827.072, F.S., defining generated child pornography as computer-generated images of a fictitious person a reasonable person would regard as a real person under 18 in sexual conduct. Knowingly possessing, controlling or intentionally viewing such material, and intentionally creating it, are third-degree felonies, each item possessed is a separate offense, and possession during a law enforcement investigation is excluded. Section 3 amends s. 92.561, F.S., requiring such material in criminal proceedings to stay secured with law enforcement, the state attorney or the court, and requiring courts to deny defendants' requests to reproduce it where the state attorney makes it reasonably available for inspection. The act takes effect July 1, 2024.

relations.note: Section 3 amends s. 92.561 to add generated child pornography to the prohibition on reproduction of material in criminal proceedings.

thresholds.measurement: Judged by whether a reasonable person would regard the depicted fictitious person as a real person of that age; no window or aggregation

thresholds.conditions: Image created, altered, adapted or modified by computer-generated means to portray a fictitious person engaged in sexual conduct

“Generated child pornography” means any image that has been created, altered, adapted, or modified by electronic, mechanical, or other computer-generated means to portray a fictitious person

At least one quarterly meeting must be joint with the Florida Cybersecurity Advisory Council.

obligations.summary: A person may not knowingly possess or control, or intentionally view, a photograph, image, data file or other presentation the person knows includes generated child pornography (each item a separate offense, third-degree felony). A person may not intentionally create generated child pornography (third-degree felony). The possession prohibition does not apply to material held as part of a law enforcement investigation.
